title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page derives the chord (secant) addition law for the elliptic curve E: Y^2 = X^3 + a1 X^2 + a2 X + a3. Here x0 = ℘(x) and x' = ℘'(x), and similarly for y and z. On the previous pages the condition x + y + z = 0 was shown to be equivalent to f = ℘' + α℘ + β having divisor {x}+{y}+{z} − 3{0_E}. That in turn is equivalent to the vanishing of the 3×3 determinant with rows (℘'(t), ℘(t), 1) for t = x, y, z (statement (41)/(42)).

Given x and y, Grothendieck now wants explicit formulas for z = −(x+y).

1. Expanding the determinant along the z-row gives (*): z'(x0 − y0) + z0(y' − x') + (x'y0 − y'x0) = 0.
2. When x0 ≠ y0, this is the line z' = λ z0 + μ (47), with λ = (x'−y')/(x0−y0) and μ = (y'x0 − x'y0)/(x0−y0).
3. Substituting into the curve equation (46) gives the cubic (48): z0^3 + (a1 − λ^2) z0^2 + (a2 − 2λμ) z0 + (a3 − μ^2) = 0.
4. This cubic has three roots, and a priori each gives a pair (z0, z') via (47). To single out the right one, he imposes z0 ≠ x0, y0 (49).

On the next page he notes that x0 and y0 are themselves roots. Vieta then gives z0 = λ^2 − a1 − x0 − y0 and z' = λ z0 + μ (51), and the formulas are extended by continuity ('prolongement') to all y ∉ ±x. Overall this is the textbook group law for a Weierstrass cubic, set up as part of a characteristic ≠ 2 treatment of moduli of elliptic curves.
errors: No mathematical errors: the sign conventions in (*) and the formulas for λ and μ are consistent with the determinant expansion.
Minor gap: the requirement that z be distinct from x and y needs a genericity hypothesis (2x+y ≠ 0, x+2y ≠ 0). This is only addressed on the next page, via the prolongation argument.

ideas.what: Collinearity determinant criterion for x+y+z=0 on a Weierstrass cubic, turned into explicit addition formulas via the secant line and Vieta's formula on the residual cubic
ideas.modern_name: Chord-tangent group law / explicit addition formulas on a Weierstrass curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weierstrass, Poincaré; standard in Silverman's AEC III.2)
ideas.where_published: Standard textbooks; not a topic of Grothendieck's published works

deep.surprise_reason: This is an entirely routine derivation of the elliptic curve addition law in the a1, a2, a3 (characteristic ≠ 2) Weierstrass form. It is pedagogical working-out with no new content.
transcription_corrections: 'L'équation (4), s'écrit' likely refers to (41) or (42), the determinant/collinearity condition from the previous page; the image is ambiguous.
Grothendieck writes ℘ in a handwritten form resembling 'p'; the previous-page transcription's 'p' and this page's '℘' denote the same function.
'3 solutions {+en z0+} de (48)': the insertion 'en z0' is written above the line, as transcribed.
